diagnostic_evidence.quote: Denote the Hilbert space on $\mathbb{H}_2^0$ as

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims the displayed set, equipped with the stated inner product, is 'the Hilbert space $L^2(\mathbb{H}_2^0)$'. The defining condition uses absolute summability $\sum|\widehat f|<\infty$ (the Wiener algebra), not $\sum|\widehat f|^2<\infty$. The set so defined is a proper subset of $L^2$ and is not complete under the stated inner product, so it is not a Hilbert space and not $L^2$. Consequently the paper's $H^\alpha(\mathbb{H}_2^0)$ is a nonstandard smaller class, and functions with non-summable but square-summable coefficients (e.g. the non-periodic test functions $f_2$, $f_3$ of Section 5, whose coefficients decay like $O(1/k)$) lie outside the defined space.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $|\widehat{f}_{(k_1,k_2)}|$ by $|\widehat{f}_{(k_1,k_2)}|^2$ in the defining condition.
issues.overall_effect: The function-space framework underlying all hypotheses ($f\in H^\alpha(\mathbb{H}_2^0)$) is misdefined; scope statements about the function class are unreliable.
issues.title: $L^2(\mathbb{H}_2^0)$ is defined via $\ell^1$-summability of Fourier coefficients, so the defined set is not the Hilbert space $L^2$
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction restores the standard space; all theorems remain valid (indeed for a larger class) with no further repair.

issues.failure_explanation: A full-column-rank matrix in $\mathbb{C}^{(2I_1+1)\times R}$ requires $R\le 2I_1+1$ (likewise $R\le 2I_2+1$). But $R=\lceil 72\ln(2(I_1+I_2)+3)/\epsilon^2\rceil$ exceeds $\min\{2I_1+1,2I_2+1\}$ over most of the stated range $0<\epsilon<1$: e.g. $I_1=I_2=10$ gives $R\ge 271>21$ for every $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, and the paper's own regime $\epsilon=10^{-7}$, $I_n=3163$ gives $R\approx 7\times 10^{16}\gg 6327$. In these regimes the asserted $\mathbf{E},\mathbf{F}$ — and hence $\widetilde{F}f$ in (t-lasso:approximation-expression-general-main), which sums $j=1,\dots,R$ — cannot exist. The proof only combines Theorems t-lasso:general-theorem-main and t-lasso:epsilonrank-main, which yield $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}$ of rank $\le R$ (factorable with $\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde{\mathbf{A}})\le R$ columns) and never establish the width-$R$ full-column-rank factorization.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, the proof is complete by combining Theorems \ref{t-lasso:general-theorem-main} and \ref{t-lasso:epsilonrank-main}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof obtains the truncation term solely from Theorem t-lasso:general-theorem-main, which gives $C\min\{I_1,I_2\}^{-\alpha}|f|_\alpha$ (and which the following remark uses correctly with min). Since $\max\{I_1,I_2\}^{-\alpha}\le\min\{I_1,I_2\}^{-\alpha}$, the stated max-version is strictly stronger than what is proved and is false in general for $I_1\ne I_2$ (e.g. a function depending only on $x_1$ has truncation error governed by $I_1$ alone, so no $\max\{I_1,I_2\}^{-\alpha}$ bound can hold). Corollary cor:added-1 repeats the same max term.
issues.overall_effect: The stated truncation-error rate of Theorem t-lasso:general-approximation-theorem-main and Corollary cor:added-1 is unproven and false for asymmetric truncation parameters.
issues.title: Truncation term claims $\max\{I_1,I_2\}^{-\alpha}$ although the invoked theorem only supports $\min\{I_1,I_2\}^{-\alpha}$
issues.why_classification: A forced local correction matching the cited theorem repairs both statements; all uses in the paper have $I_1=I_2$, so no downstream content changes.

issues.failure_explanation: $\widetilde{F}f-Ff$ is a trigonometric polynomial whose coefficients are the entries of $\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*$; the exponentials are orthonormal under the stated inner product, so by the paper's own Parseval identity $\|\widetilde{F}f-Ff\|_{L^2}=\|\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*\|_F$ exactly. The claimed inequality with $\|\cdot\|_{\max}$ is false as soon as the coefficient error has more than one significant entry: e.g. $\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*=\delta\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top$ gives $\|\widetilde{F}f-Ff\|_{L^2}=\delta\sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}>\delta$. The correct conversion costs a factor $\sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}$, so the theorem's second term $\epsilon\|\mathbf{A}\|_2$ is unproven and false in general (for $\mathbf{A}$ with flat spectrum, any rank-$R=O(\log/\epsilon^2)$ factorization has Frobenius coefficient error far exceeding $\epsilon\|\mathbf{A}\|_2$); the provable term is $\epsilon\sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}\|\mathbf{A}\|_2$. Corollary cor:added-1 transfers the max-norm CUR bound directly to the $L^2$ error and inherits the same missing factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the step by $\|\widetilde{F}f-Ff\|_{L^2}=\|\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*\|_F\le\sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}\|\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*\|_{\max}$ and weaken the second term of both results accordingly (to $\epsilon\sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}\|\mathbf{A}\|_2$ and to $\sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}\sqrt{1+S_2}\sqrt{1+S_2/(S_1-S_2+1)}\sigma_{S_2+1}(\mathbf{A})$).
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative error guarantees of Theorem t-lasso:general-approximation-theorem-main and Corollary cor:added-1 (the $\epsilon$-scaling of the approximation-error term) are unreliable.
issues.title: Invalid Parseval step: the $L^2$ function error is bounded by the max-norm of the coefficient error
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained (one inequality plus restating one term in each of two results) and leaves a structurally comparable bound, but it necessarily degrades the stated $\epsilon$-accuracy by an unavoidable dimension-dependent factor, so it is more than a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a tolerance $0<\tau<1$, and the maximum number of iterations $K$.

issues.failure_explanation: With the disjunction, the loop body executes whenever ${\rm tol}>\tau$ or $k\le K$. Since $k$ starts at 0, $k\le K$ holds for the first $K+1$ executions regardless of ${\rm tol}$, so the algorithm always performs at least $K+1$ iterations: $K$ acts as a minimum, contradicting the stated input 'the maximum number of iterations $K$'. Moreover, once $k>K$ the loop continues as long as ${\rm tol}>\tau$, so $K$ never bounds the iteration count and the algorithm can run unboundedly; adaptive early termination never fires before $k>K$. The same condition appears in t-lasso:alg2-main and t-lasso:alg1:app-main.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change 'or' to 'and' in the while-conditions of all three algorithms.
issues.overall_effect: The iteration-count contract of all three algorithms fails; the stated integral/complexity analyses (premised on termination at the stopping condition with $K$ as a cap) do not describe the printed control flow.

issues.failure_explanation: Zeroing $\mathbf{G}_{1k}$ and $\mathbf{G}_{2k}$ only postpones work: those coefficients are entries of $\mathbf{C}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ and are still required in the final step. The correct total is $(2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-1-4Kb_1b_2$ (the block-diagonal core costs $1+4Kb_1b_2$ integrals; $\mathbf{C}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ then require all remaining entries).
